title: HX-101 vs docetaxel in 2L EGFR-mutant NSCLC
indication: EGFR-mutant NSCLC, second line after osimertinib

baseRate.class: Phase 3 oncology, OS primary, post-3G TKI

summary: Randomised open-label study in a post-osimertinib population. OS primary with a 4.5-month improvement target; enrolment assumes 18% annual attrition from competing trials.

designFlags.title: Comparator is no longer standard of care in the enrolling geographies
designFlags.detail: Docetaxel is defensible historically but increasingly replaced by platinum-based rechallenge and ADC-containing regimens in the sites listed. A positive OS result against docetaxel may not support the intended label narrative.

designFlags.title: OS effect size assumes a larger benefit than the observed Phase 2 tail
designFlags.detail: The 4.5-month delta exceeds the upper bound implied by the Phase 2 survival curve once crossover is accounted for. Power falls below 80% if the true delta is 3.0 months.

designFlags.title: Enrolment assumption ignores two competing registrational studies
designFlags.detail: Two trials in the same line of therapy are recruiting in the same countries; screen-failure and activation delays are likely under-modelled.

evidence.claim: Guideline-concordant second-line therapy after third-generation TKI failure is heterogeneous and increasingly ADC-based.
evidence.span: Post-TKI progression is managed with platinum rechallenge, ADC monotherapy, or trial enrolment; docetaxel is a residual option.

evidence.claim: Historic docetaxel control arms overstate the incremental benefit of new agents.
evidence.span: Control-arm performance in post-TKI NSCLC has improved over the last decade, compressing apparent treatment effects.

evidence.claim: Phase 2 tail estimates for this asset imply a 2.6–3.4 month OS delta, not 4.5.
evidence.span: Restricted mean survival difference at 24 months was 2.9 months (95% CI 1.4–4.4).

evidence.claim: Two registrational trials compete for the same second-line population in the same countries.
evidence.span: Both studies list overlapping sites and identical eligibility in the post-osimertinib setting.

evidence.claim: Crossover to subsequent therapy dilutes OS effects in open-label designs.
evidence.span: Post-progression therapy differed between arms in 41% of assessed studies, attenuating OS estimates.

title: NW-77 in HFpEF with exercise limitation
summary: Dose-ranging study with a functional primary endpoint. Includes a diuretic-stable subgroup and a broad eligibility window that admits both obese and non-obese phenotypes.

designFlags.title: Functional endpoint has weak regulatory and predictive standing in HFpEF
designFlags.detail: 6MWD changes have repeatedly failed to track with outcomes in this population. A positive result may not de-risk a Phase 3, and a null result may not kill the asset — the study cannot discriminate.

designFlags.title: Phenotype heterogeneity dilutes the expected effect
designFlags.detail: Mixing obese and non-obese HFpEF without stratification assumes a shared mechanism; prior programmes show effect concentration in one phenotype.

designFlags.title: Placebo run-in is absent, so background-therapy changes are uncontrolled
designFlags.detail: Diuretic adjustment during the run-in phase is not protocolised, adding variance to the primary endpoint.

evidence.claim: 6MWD improvements have not reliably predicted outcome benefit in HFpEF.
evidence.span: Across assessed trials, 6MWD change explained little of the variance in subsequent CV death or hospitalisation effects.

evidence.claim: Regulators have accepted functional endpoints only with supportive outcome trends.
evidence.span: Functional primary endpoints were accepted where secondary outcome measures moved in the same direction.

evidence.claim: Obese and non-obese HFpEF differ in treatment response.
evidence.span: Treatment effects were concentrated in the obese phenotype in two of three assessed programmes.

evidence.claim: Unprotocolised diuretic changes add measurable variance to exercise endpoints.
evidence.span: Sites reporting ad-lib diuretic titration showed wider 6MWD variance than protocolised sites.

title: AN-4 in early Alzheimer's disease
summary: Two-arm study with 18-month cognitive primary. Site mix includes high-placebo-response regions; no enrichment for tau status.

designFlags.title: Placebo response in the site mix can swamp the expected effect
designFlags.detail: Regions with historically high CDR-SB placebo drift are over-represented. The assumed 0.45-point delta is within the range of site-level placebo variability.

designFlags.title: No tau enrichment reduces the expected treatment effect
designFlags.detail: Amyloid confirmation alone admits a population where target engagement is unlikely to translate; tau-PET or plasma p-tau enrichment would raise the prior.

designFlags.title: 18-month duration is at the short end for CDR-SB separation
designFlags.detail: Separation in comparable programmes emerged between 18 and 24 months; the study may read out before the effect stabilises.

evidence.claim: Placebo CDR-SB drift varies materially by region and site experience.
evidence.span: Adjusted placebo change ranged from 0.2 to 0.9 points across regions in pooled early-AD studies.

evidence.claim: Trials with higher placebo drift show smaller measured treatment effects.
evidence.span: Each 0.3-point increase in placebo change was associated with a 0.18-point reduction in estimated effect.

evidence.claim: Tau status enriches for cognitive progression and treatment response.
evidence.span: Progression rates were approximately doubled in tau-positive participants versus amyloid-only selection.

evidence.claim: CDR-SB separation in comparable programmes emerges later than 18 months.
evidence.span: In two assessed programmes, curves separated after month 18 and continued to diverge to month 24.

title: MR-9 in Fabry disease nephropathy

baseRate.class: Phase 2 rare disease, slope endpoint, single arm

summary: Single-arm study using historical control for eGFR slope. Enrolment is limited by genotype and treatment status; two dose levels with unequal allocation.

designFlags.title: Historical control is not exchangeable with the enrolled population
designFlags.detail: The historical cohort was younger and less proteinuric; slope comparisons will be confounded by baseline progression rate.

designFlags.title: 12-month slope is noisy at this sample size
designFlags.detail: With 60 participants split across doses, the confidence interval on slope difference will likely span clinically distinct scenarios.

designFlags.title: Unequal dose allocation weakens the dose-response read
designFlags.detail: A 2:1 allocation with an open-label design limits interpretation of the low-dose arm.

evidence.claim: Historical Fabry cohorts differ systematically from contemporarily enrolled patients.
evidence.span: Historical controls were younger and had lower baseline proteinuria than recently enrolled cohorts.

evidence.claim: Baseline proteinuria predicts eGFR slope and confounds external comparisons.
evidence.span: Baseline UPCR explained a substantial share of slope variance in untreated cohorts.

evidence.claim: Twelve-month eGFR slope has wide uncertainty at n<100.
evidence.span: Simulated 95% intervals spanned both benefit and harm at the planned sample size.

evidence.claim: Open-label unequal allocation biases patient-reported and clinician-assessed endpoints.
evidence.span: Open-label allocation was associated with differential concomitant therapy changes.

title: CB-2 vs vedolizumab in moderate-to-severe UC
indication: Ulcerative colitis, inadequate response to anti-TNF

baseRate.class: Phase 3 immunology, active comparator, remission endpoint

summary: Head-to-head non-inferiority design against vedolizumab with a 10% margin. Central reading is used for endoscopy; corticosteroid tapering is protocolised.

designFlags.title: Non-inferiority margin is wider than the historical effect of the comparator
designFlags.detail: A 10% margin exceeds the conservative fraction of the vedolizumab effect, so a positive result may not establish a clinically meaningful benefit.

designFlags.title: Screen failure and prior biologic exposure will slow enrolment
designFlags.detail: The anti-TNF-refractory population is heavily recruited and protocol exclusions are broad; the enrolment curve assumes 1.4 patients per site-month.

designFlags.title: Steroid tapering rules interact with the remission definition
designFlags.detail: The primary endpoint requires steroid-free remission; tapering failures will be counted as non-remitters and may bias against the experimental arm if tapering is faster there.

evidence.claim: Non-inferiority margins should preserve at least half the comparator's established effect.
evidence.span: Guidance favours margins that preserve a substantial fraction of the reference effect, with justification.

evidence.claim: A 10% margin exceeds half the historical vedolizumab remission effect.
evidence.span: Placebo-adjusted week-52 remission differences clustered below 20 percentage points.

evidence.claim: Anti-TNF-refractory UC populations are saturated with competing trials.
evidence.span: Median site-month enrolment in comparable studies was below the assumed rate.

evidence.claim: Steroid-free remission definitions penalise arms with faster tapering schedules.
evidence.span: Faster taper schedules produced more tapering failures without differences in endoscopic improvement.

title: SB-5 in MASH with F2–F3 fibrosis
endpoint: Fibrosis improvement ≥1 stage without worsening of MASH
summary: Biopsy-based histological endpoint with central reading. Eligibility requires a recent biopsy; two readers adjudicate discordance.

designFlags.title: Histological endpoint has high reader variability at this effect size
designFlags.detail: Inter-reader agreement on one-stage fibrosis change is modest; the expected 12% absolute difference is close to the noise floor.

designFlags.title: Class-level failures reduce the prior for this mechanism
designFlags.detail: Several programmes targeting the same pathway failed on fibrosis endpoints despite metabolic improvement.

designFlags.title: Biopsy requirement narrows enrolment and selects advanced patients
designFlags.detail: Requiring a biopsy within 6 months excludes patients and may skew the population toward faster progressors.

evidence.claim: One-stage fibrosis change has limited inter-reader reproducibility.
evidence.span: Agreement on stage change was moderate, with discordance concentrated at stage boundaries.

evidence.claim: Small absolute differences are indistinguishable from reader noise without adjudication.
evidence.span: Adjudicated reads reduced but did not eliminate misclassification at a 12% effect size.

evidence.claim: Metabolic improvement has not reliably translated into fibrosis benefit in this class.
evidence.span: Several programmes improved steatohepatitis scores without meeting fibrosis endpoints.

evidence.claim: Biopsy-based eligibility selects more advanced and faster-progressing patients.
evidence.span: Biopsy-confirmed cohorts showed higher progression rates than imaging-selected cohorts.
